problem: Prior embodied QA/assistance work uses simulated agents or AI-AI interaction and gives no large-scale human data on when people recall vs. navigate vs. ask for help about a visually experienced environment. Without such data, assistants (e.g., AR glasses) cannot model what a human has encoded or predict when they need help.
motivation: All-day AR assistants need a 'theory of mind' for human perception and memory to intervene helpfully without being intrusive. Human behavior data in realistic 3D scenes is needed to build human-aligned representations and priors for when assistance is requested.
key_idea: Introduce the Memory Question Answering (MemQA) task and the Visually Grounded Assistant dataset, where humans view a Matterport3D fly-through, then answer EQA-style questions by guessing, self-navigating or paying time for an oracle assistant, and predict this behavior from hand-crafted exposure features.
insight: Simple hand-crafted features predict human correctness only modestly (best AUC 0.67, MLP), and predict self-navigation at chance (about 0.50-0.51). Random-forest feature importance shows fly-through length, time of first exposure and spatial exposure of the object matter most, while object semantics (GloVe embeddings) and question type matter little. This suggests the models lack spatial-map and path-complexity features.
method: MemQA task: participants watch a ~70 s fly-through of a Matterport3D building (panoramic RGB in a Matterport-simulator-based interface on AMT), then answer 4 questions within 2.5 min via drop-down answers.

Three answer strategies: answer immediately, navigate themselves, or request an oracle assistant that teleports them to the answer location at a time cost of 10+ s proportional to distance; monetary bonus for correct answers.

Question generation: programmatic EQA templates on Matterport3D meshes, extended with existence, count and comparison types (11 types); ~20% filtered after a crowd-sourced annotation verification study.

Fly-through generation: sample 4 questions about different objects, compute the shortest path visiting the needed locations, add short random trajectories at start and end, and keep only 45-75 s paths.

Exposure features: Habitat instance and semantic segmentation give time of first exposure, temporal exposure and spatial exposure (total pixels) of the primary object, plus fly-through length, question type and a 5-D PCA-reduced GloVe object embedding (10 features total).

Baselines: four binary classifiers (correct, no navigation, self navigation, assistance) using RF (10 trees), MLP (1 hidden layer of 100) and RBF-SVM from scikit-learn, trained on 80% of the data and tested on 20% with disjoint questions.

setting.backbone: Scikit-learn Random Forest / MLP / SVM on 10 hand-crafted features (GloVe+PCA object embedding)
setting.training_data: VGA dataset: 1250 unique MemQA tasks, 6275 human annotations from 412 AMT workers (80/20 split by question)
setting.observation: human participants see panoramic RGB from Matterport3D; models use simulator-derived segmentation-based exposure features and no raw pixels
setting.action_space: human choices: answer directly, self-navigate on the Matterport nav graph, or request oracle assistance (this is a prediction task, not agent control)
setting.privileged: Habitat semantic/instance segmentation and annotated mesh for feature extraction; oracle assistant uses the annotated 3D mesh and questions

numbers_note: No navigation-benchmark numbers; only AUC-ROC of behavior-prediction classifiers (MLP: no navigation 0.57, self navigation 0.51, assistance 0.59, answered correctly 0.67) which do not fit any canonical benchmark.
results: Human accuracy averages 70.34% (random chance 29.08%), 58.34% of annotations used assistance, and 25.23% of questions had assistance requests. Best baseline AUC-ROC is 0.67 (MLP) for correctness, 0.59 for assistance and 0.57 for no navigation. Self-navigation is not predicted better than chance.
limitations: Baselines are weak with hand-selected features and only single-object question types (comparison and count questions omitted), with no spatial-map or path features.
Assistant is a passive oracle and only the single-question prediction task is modeled, not the time-step-level second task.
Fly-through is passive and ~70 s in Matterport scenes on AMT, so generalization to real AR everyday memory is unclear.
compares_to: RF vs MLP vs SVM baselines
